integration.scope: IO, authority, entry and task integration as configured by run-musl-io.py

residency_scan.interpretation: Source checks PTE presence, not write readiness. The adaptive stream scans up to 64 resident pages after a demand fault; zero-page mappings are present but later writes still need COW. Flat counts establish substantial scanning work, not an inclusive causal attribution or exact invocation count.
residency_scan.next_experiment: Bound repeated scans or distinguish readiness for the requested access; retain Linux COW/permissions, arena identity, locking, revocation and copy holds. Keep separate from access-direction switch.

excluded_pilots: result and extra-result: long GCC cmdlines truncated at kernel COMMAND_LINE_SIZE=512; supposed no-ahead GCC actually used default ahead64. Initial IO/race access option was truncated and remained off. Superseded by verified cohorts with length guards and guest readback.
Earlier tag-first probe used identical pointers and immediate verification; superseded by distinct pointers, untouched-page checks and delayed verification.
limitations: QEMU instruction attempts, not hardware cycles or speedup.
Two GCC samples per arm per ahead setting; one microbenchmark sample per configuration.
Microbenchmark totals include startup/exit; RSS is whole-process peak.
Plain and Capstone compiler/libc differ; policy effects use unchanged binaries within the native arm.
Armed SIGSEGV smoke tests do not verify precise fault PC/cause; existing race oracles are stronger separate checks.
Sysfs counters include measurement-shell activity; suppressed-read counter counts attempts, not unique pages.
No new full SPEC, multi-hart or FPGA qualification.
Default-off experiment; no claim that removing speculative writes is a general optimization.
